title.value: Sample Compression Unleashed: New Generalization Bounds for Real Valued Losses
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper: introducing new generalization bounds related to sample compression for real valued losses.
title.quote: Sample Compression Unleashed: New Generalization Bounds for Real Valued Losses

analysis.description: The paper introduces new theoretical bounds for sample compression in the context of real-valued losses. Using the Pick-To-Learn (P2L) meta-algorithm, the authors empirically demonstrate the tightness and versatility of these bounds across different models, including random forests and neural networks. The framework aims to provide generalization guarantees without depending on the number of learnable parameters.

type.justification: The paper is focused on proposing new theoretical bounds for sample compression in the context of real-valued losses.
type.quote: The sample compression theory provides generalization guarantees for predictors that can be fully defined using a subset of the training dataset and a (short) message string, generally defined as a binary sequence. Previous works provided generalization bounds for the zero-one loss, which is restrictive notably when applied to deep learning approaches. In this paper, we present a general framework for deriving new sample compression bounds that hold for real-valued unbounded losses.

name.justification: The paper's focus is on developing theoretical results related to sample compression and generalization bounds, which is a part of theoretical machine learning research.
name.quote: By leveraging proof techniques from the PAC-Bayesian literature, we extend the framework to real-valued losses and open the way to obtaining bounds directly for the cross-entropy loss [45] and unbounded losses [20, 10, 46], for example under the sub-Gaussian assumption.

is_executed.quote: Finally, we train deep neural networks and random forests with the Pick-To-Learn meta-algorithm [43], an algorithm that modifies the training loop of a model to yield a sample-compressed predictor, and assess the tightness of our bounds in different settings.

is_compared.quote: We obtain tight bounds simultaneously on the zero-one loss and the cross-entropy loss, demonstrating that our new theorem is independent of the number of parameters of the model.
